title: The Vector and Canonical Components of the Momentum Operator in 3D Euclidean Space Spanned by General Curvilinear Coordinates
abstract: We construct the Hermitian vector and canonical components of the momentum operator in 3D Euclidean space spanned by general curvilinear coordinates (GCC's) using a simple, natural and unified approach based on identifying the momentum operator in any coordinate system as mass times the velocity operator. When this latter is calculated by applying the Heisenberg equation of motion, it returns ($-i\hbar$ times) the gradient operator plus an additional zero-valued sum, which when distributed among the components of the gradient, it makes each the Hermitian vector component of the momentum operator in GCC's. The canonical components follow immediately upon symmetrizing each of these vector components in the corresponding base vector. For accessability by wider audiences, we first develop the formalism for the simple polar coordinates and then we develop the case for GCC's.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous theoretical framework to define the momentum operator in general curvilinear coordinates. By relating the momentum to the velocity operator via the Heisenberg equation, the authors construct Hermitian vector and canonical components that correctly account for geometric curvature effects. This provides essential mathematical machinery for quantum mechanics on curved spaces.
main_problem: The construction of the Hermitian vector and canonical components of the momentum operator ($\vec{p}$) in 3D Euclidean space when expressed using general curvilinear coordinates (GCC's).
main_result: A unified, natural approach is developed showing that while individual coordinate derivatives are problematic, the full momentum operator $\vec{p}$ remains Hermitian due to cancellation of boundary terms.
method: The method utilizes the Heisenberg equation of motion applied to the position operator ($\vec{r}$) and identifies $\vec{p} \propto m\dot{\vec{r}}$ to derive corrected, Hermitian vector components ($\vec{p}_H$) before projecting them onto canonical forms ($p_H^a$).
model_or_system: The study is purely theoretical, focusing on the mathematical structure of quantum mechanics in curved coordinate systems. The underlying physical system involves a particle whose Hamiltonian includes the Laplace-Beltrami operator.
key_observables: Hermiticity of $\vec{p}$ and its components; canonical commutation relations $[q^a, p_H^b] = i\hbar \delta^a_b$.
main_assumptions: Standard physical boundary conditions (e.g., square-integrability) are assumed for the necessary integration by parts to prove Hermiticity.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the text develops explicit forms for operators like $\vec{p}_H$ and $p_H^a$ in specific coordinate systems (e.g., polar/spherical).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem by noting that naive momentum components fail Hermiticity; it then derives a general procedure using the Heisenberg equation to construct $\vec{p}_H$; this is demonstrated explicitly for simple cases like polar coordinates before generalizing the formalism to arbitrary GCC's.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental mathematical tools necessary for correctly formulating quantum mechanics on curved manifolds, which is crucial when modeling physical systems whose geometry cannot be approximated by flat Euclidean space.
